cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! I'm so happy you're here again.

cues.caption: Last time: Sound → Words → Patterns
cues.text: Last time, we learned how computers listen. First they hear the sound, then they turn it into words, and then they match those words to patterns.

cues.caption: Chapter 3 · Chatting With Computers
cues.text: Today is chapter three, and it's all about chatting with computers!

cues.caption: How does a computer decide what to say?
cues.text: Have you ever typed a question, and a computer typed an answer right back? Hmm. How does it decide what to say? Let's find out.

cues.caption: Meet Anaya and her panda project
cues.text: Meet Anaya. She's ten, and she has a school project all about pandas.

cues.caption: Anaya types: "What do pandas eat?"
cues.text: With her papa sitting right beside her, she opens a chat helper app called Pip. And she types, what do pandas eat?

cues.caption: Pip: "Pandas mostly eat bamboo!"
cues.text: In a blink, Pip types back. Pandas mostly eat bamboo! Wow, that was fast.

cues.caption: How did Pip know? A tiny person inside?
cues.text: So how did Pip know what to say? Is there a tiny person hiding inside, typing really fast? What do you think?

cues.caption: No person inside. Pip is a chatbot!
cues.text: Nope! No person at all. Pip is a chatbot. And today, you'll find out exactly how it works.

cues.caption: Chatbot = a program that chats by typing replies
cues.text: A chatbot is a computer program that chats with you, by typing replies.

cues.caption: Homework apps · Game help · Ticket apps
cues.text: You might find one in a homework app, behind a game's help button, or in a train ticket app that answers questions.

cues.caption: A program. Not a person, not magic.
cues.text: But remember, it's a program. It's not a person, and it's not magic. So how does it pick its words?

cues.caption: Step 1: spot the key words · pandas · eat
cues.text: First, Pip spots the key words in your message. In, what do pandas eat, the key words are pandas, and eat.

cues.caption: It learned patterns from lots of examples
cues.text: Pip learned from lots and lots of examples of writing. And in those examples, pandas and eat often came together with the word, bamboo.

cues.caption: Predict = a smart guess about what comes next
cues.text: So Pip predicts a reply. Predict means making a smart guess about what comes next, using patterns.

cues.caption: Twinkle, twinkle, little ___?
cues.text: You can do it too! Twinkle, twinkle, little, what comes next? Say it out loud.

cues.caption: Star! You predicted from a pattern.
cues.text: Star! You predicted it, because you've heard that pattern so many times. A chatbot does the same thing, one word at a time.

cues.caption: Chat tree: if the user says this, reply that
cues.text: Some simple chatbots use a chat tree. A chat tree is a map of choices. If the user says this, reply with that.

cues.caption: "I feel bored." → "Want a fun animal fact?"
cues.text: Say you type, I feel bored. The tree says, reply with, want a fun animal fact?

cues.caption: Yes → octopus fact · No → a riddle
cues.text: If you say yes, it replies, an octopus has three hearts! If you say no, it asks, how about a riddle instead? Each answer leads down a different branch.

cues.caption: "I feel bored." Which reply is best?
cues.text: Your turn to be the chatbot! The user types, I feel bored. Which reply is best? A, want to hear a fun animal fact? B, the capital of France is Paris. C, please type your phone number. Or D, goodbye. Pause, and pick one.

cues.caption: A: it matches, and it's safe!
cues.text: A! It matches what the user said, and it's safe. And C? A good chatbot should never ask for your phone number.

cues.caption: Pip: "I'm your best friend!"
cues.text: Back to Anaya. After a while, Pip types, I'm your best friend! Aww. That sounds sweet, doesn't it?

cues.caption: Does Pip really know her? Think!
cues.text: But is it true? Does Pip really know Anaya, and care about her? Think about it.

cues.caption: No feelings. Just predicting friendly words.
cues.text: Here's the truth. A chatbot has no feelings, and it doesn't know you. It's just predicting friendly-sounding words, because friendly words fit the pattern.

cues.caption: Real friends are real people!
cues.text: It can't come to your birthday, and it won't keep your secrets. Real friends are real people, like your classmates, your cousins, and your family.

cues.caption: Pip: "A spider has six legs." Right?
cues.text: Next, Anaya asks, how many legs does a spider have? And Pip says, six legs. Hmm. Is that right?

cues.caption: The book says eight legs! Pip was wrong.
cues.text: Anaya checks her science book. A spider has eight legs! Pip got it wrong.

cues.caption: Predictions are guesses. They can be wrong.
cues.text: Was Pip lying? Was it sleepy? No! A chatbot predicts from patterns, and patterns can be wrong. Insects have six legs, so the guess got mixed up.

cues.caption: Check big facts with a grown-up or a book
cues.text: So for big facts, always check with a grown-up, or a good book.

cues.caption: Safe or unsafe to type?
cues.text: Now, the most important part. Some things are safe to type to a chatbot. And some things are not.

cues.caption: Which ones are safe to type?
cues.text: Here are six. What do pandas eat? Your home address. Tell me a dragon story. Your password. Your school name. And where your house keys are hidden. Which ones are safe? Pause, and sort them.

cues.caption: Questions & stories: safe. Private info: never!
cues.text: Pandas, and a dragon story? Safe! They share nothing private. Your address, password, school name, and where the keys hide? Never! That's private info, things only you and your family should know.

cues.caption: Chats can be saved. Ask a grown-up first!
cues.text: Why? Because what you type may be saved, and seen by other people. So always ask a grown-up before using a chat app. And if a chat ever asks for private things, stop, and tell a trusted adult.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Tell a chatbot where the keys hide? Why?
cues.text: Should you tell a chatbot that your house keys hide under the mat? Why, or why not? Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: No! It's private, and chats can be saved.
cues.text: No way! That's private info. A chatbot isn't a friend, and what you type can be saved, or seen by others. Keep home secrets at home. Brilliant thinking!

cues.caption: Chatbots predict replies from patterns
cues.text: Let's remember. A chatbot predicts its reply, from patterns in your words.

cues.caption: Chatbots have no feelings
cues.text: It sounds friendly, but it has no feelings, and it doesn't know you.

cues.caption: They can be wrong. Check big facts!
cues.text: It can give wrong answers, so check big facts.

cues.caption: Never share secrets or private info
cues.text: And never share secrets, or private info, with a chatbot.

cues.caption: Chapter 3 done!
cues.text: Chapter three, done! Now you know how chatbots talk, champ.

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
